“I suspect that nobody would have given the skull of his father or his grandfather as a gift to another person.” The Naga people once practised headhunting, severing the heads of enemies as trophies, but also kept the heads of their own chiefs “at the centre of the villages”, and one of the remains is a chief’s head, said anthropologist Dolly Kikon, a member of Nagaland’s Lotha-Naga community.
